questions.scenario: Your school club is collecting money for a big trip. How do you want to manage the funds?

options.text: I want to design a simple app interface where students can just tap once to pay and see their contribution.
I want to create a digital 'club token' that students can trade and use for payments automatically.
I want to build a complex spreadsheet with formulas that predict exactly if we will have enough money by next month.
I want to set up strict rules and audit the accounts to make sure no one can fake a payment or steal from the fund.

questions.scenario: You are playing a massive online multiplayer game with its own economy. What do you do?

options.text: I figure out how to make trading items between players smoother and less frustrating.
I look into how the game's virtual currency is coded and if I can mine or generate it automatically.
I track the price history of rare items and use that data to buy low and sell high for massive profits.
I spend my time hunting down scammers and figuring out how they trick players into losing their gold.

questions.scenario: When you use a payment app like Google Pay, Paytm, or Apple Pay, what goes through your mind?

options.text: I appreciate the satisfying 'ding' sound and the cool animation that plays when a payment is successful.
I wonder how the technology bypasses traditional slow banks to move digital money instantly.
I think about the algorithms running in the background, analyzing my spending habits to suggest loans.
I think about the encryption and security layers that stop hackers from intercepting my bank password.

questions.scenario: A friend pitches a brand new business idea to you. What is your immediate reaction?

options.text: I start drawing out what the app for the business would look like to make it super user-friendly.
I suggest they raise funds by launching a decentralized digital asset or NFT.
I calculate the exact probability of their success based on current market data and profit margins.
I point out all the legal, privacy, and security loopholes they need to fix before launching.

questions.scenario: If you could instantly have a superpower, which one would you choose?

options.text: The ability to instantly make any confusing or difficult task super easy for anyone to understand.
The ability to teleport instantly anywhere in the world without borders or central control.
The ability to see 5 seconds into the future so I can win every bet or trade.
The ability to be completely invisible and immune to any kind of physical or digital attack.

questions.scenario: You are watching a heist or robbery movie. What part of the plot interests you the most?

options.text: Noticing how outdated and clunky the bank's systems and computer interfaces look.
Wondering why they are stealing heavy paper money instead of untraceable digital assets.
Calculating exactly how much the stolen gold weighs and how dumping it will crash market prices.
Focusing on exactly how the hackers bypassed the vault's biometrics and security cameras.

questions.scenario: You are buying something from a new online website. What is your habit?

options.text: I get annoyed if the checkout process takes more than two clicks or requires too much typing.
I look to see if they accept alternative decentralized payment methods instead of just credit cards.
I notice how the website's algorithm uses my browsing history to dynamically change prices or recommendations.
I double-check the URL, look for the padlock icon, and ensure it's not a phishing scam.

questions.scenario: How do you prefer to handle your pocket money or savings?

options.text: I categorize it in a neat, colorful budgeting app to easily see where my money goes.
I am curious about investing a small part of it into digital currencies or new tech projects.
I track every penny in a spreadsheet and project exactly how much I will have by the end of the year.
I divide it and hide it in multiple secure places so if I lose one stash, I don't lose it all.

questions.scenario: Your school is hosting a Tech & Innovation Fair. What project do you present?

options.text: A design prototype for a wearable smart-band that lets students pay for canteen food instantly.
A demonstration of a basic 'smart contract' code running on a test network.
An AI model that predicts student test scores based on data like sleep and study hours.
A live hacking demonstration showing how easy it is to steal data on open Wi-Fi, and how to prevent it.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube video are you most likely to fall down a rabbit hole watching at night?

options.text: Reviews of the sleekest new apps, tech gadgets, and user interface designs.
Explainers on Web3, decentralized technology, and the future of internet money.
Videos explaining the complex math and algorithms behind massive stock market crashes.
Documentaries or true crime stories about famous hackers and massive digital heists.

FinTech_Product_Manager.title: FinTech Product Manager
FinTech_Product_Manager.primary_match_text: You are creative and user-focused. You hate complex, frustrating systems and love designing solutions that make money management easy, beautiful, and accessible for everyday people.
FinTech_Product_Manager.day_in_the_life: Working with designers and engineers to build the next viral payment app, deciding what new features to add, and ensuring the user experience is flawless.
FinTech_Product_Manager.alternative_match_text: Because you understand what people want and how to make apps easy to use, working as a UX/UI Designer for financial apps is a fantastic backup plan.
FinTech_Product_Manager.roadmap: Any stream in 11th/12th (Commerce or Science preferred). Pursue a BBA, B.Tech, or degree in Design, and focus on Product Management and User Experience (UX).

Blockchain_Developer.title: Blockchain & Crypto Engineer
Blockchain_Developer.primary_match_text: You are a tech visionary who loves the idea of a decentralized future. You are fascinated by new technologies that challenge the traditional banking system and give power back to the user.
Blockchain_Developer.day_in_the_life: Writing complex code for smart contracts, building decentralized finance (DeFi) applications, and creating secure digital assets on a blockchain network.
Blockchain_Developer.alternative_match_text: If you love the tech but want a broader field, becoming a general Software Engineer for financial startups is a highly lucrative alternative.
Blockchain_Developer.roadmap: Take PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Math) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Computer Science or IT, and start learning specific languages like Solidity or Rust.

Financial_Data_Scientist.title: Financial Data Scientist (Quant)
Financial_Data_Scientist.primary_match_text: You are highly analytical and driven by logic. You love finding hidden patterns in massive amounts of information and using math and AI to predict future trends.
Financial_Data_Scientist.day_in_the_life: Building artificial intelligence models that analyze millions of market transactions per second to predict stock prices, approve loans, or automate trading.
Financial_Data_Scientist.alternative_match_text: With your strong math and analytical skills, working as a traditional Actuary or Financial Analyst is a very stable and high-paying backup plan.
Financial_Data_Scientist.roadmap: Take PCM (with Math) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Data Science/Computer Science or a degree in Statistics/Applied Mathematics.

Cybersecurity_Fraud_Analyst.title: Cybersecurity & Fraud Analyst
Cybersecurity_Fraud_Analyst.primary_match_text: You are protective, detail-oriented, and love solving puzzles. You have a hacker's mindset but want to use it to defend people, stop criminals, and keep digital money safe.
Cybersecurity_Fraud_Analyst.day_in_the_life: Monitoring digital payment networks for suspicious activity, tracking down cybercriminals attempting to steal funds, and hacking your own company's systems to find and fix weaknesses.
Cybersecurity_Fraud_Analyst.alternative_match_text: Since you love protecting systems and solving mysteries, working in Digital Forensics or as an Ethical Hacker across any industry is a perfect fit.
Cybersecurity_Fraud_Analyst.roadmap: Take PCM or Commerce with Math in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Tech in Computer Science with a specialization in Cybersecurity, or get certifications in Ethical Hacking.
